still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month on the box, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has still approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US. Generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.
The 503B compounding exclusion finalised in 2026 still stands, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels.

The Sep 2027 tri-agency guidance letting wellness programmes tie up to a 30% premium differential to verified adherence or BMI is unchanged, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state law of its kind.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 32.0% ever-used minus 25.7% current leaves 6.3% of adults who have used the drugs and are off them now. 42% of ever-users have cycled, which is 13.4 points: ~11.5 points are current users on at least their second course (~45% of current users) and ~1.9 points cycled before and are off again. That fits one-year persistence of about one-third and ~40% restarting within a year, compounded, with new starts outpacing stops. Age bands weighted by adult population (20/33/24/23%) give ~25.7%. 25.7% of ~265M adults is ~68M users. Payer mix: commercial ~29% (~19.7M, mostly diabetes, cardiac, OSA and alcohol-use codes), Medicare ~17% (~11.6M), Medicaid ~8% (~5.4M), legitimate cash (TrumpRx, LillyDirect, NovoCare) ~34% (~23.2M), compounded, imported or counterfeit ~12% (~8.2M). The three groups that drove growth are cash orals at lower maintenance prices, retatrutide since Apr 2029, and alcohol-use prescribing, which mental-health parity in commercial plans and mandatory Medicaid/Part D coverage for non-excluded indications pull in after the Feb 2030 approval. Off-drug populations: ~16.7M adults who used and stopped (many regaining, older women overrepresented among regainers with low bone density). Adult obesity is ~32.9%, down from 34.8%. About 19% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug: uninsured, priced out, older adults without a qualifying code, or refusers. Under-18 use (1.2%) is concentrated at ages 12–17. Roughly 1 in 4 upper-income adolescents with severe obesity is on a drug, versus about 1 in 14 in the bottom third.

access.public_coverage: Medicare Part D still excludes weight loss by statute but covers incretins for diabetes, cardiovascular, CKD, OSA, MASH, dementia risk (tirzepatide, PA) and, since Feb 2030, alcohol use disorder (oral semaglutide). The negotiated semaglutide price (~$274/month) has applied since 2027. ~11.6M Medicare users × ~$250 average net/month × 12 ≈ $35B a year in Part D spending. Medicaid: 9 states still cover weight management at the $245 rate. All states must cover the AUD indication under rebate rules, usually with prior authorisation and a documented AUDIT score. The Bridge pilot was not revived.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide costs $5–35/month, Chinese generics are similar, and Canadian generics run CAD 55–90. Generic tirzepatide is not yet legal in most markets, but Chinese 'research peptide' tirzepatide and retatrutide are widely sold online. India and China supply most of the world's semaglutide volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Business Group on Health (Jan 2030) finds 31% of large employers cover weight management, down from 44%. Another ~10% cover it only through adherence-verified metabolic tracks. Coverage concentrates on diabetes/cardiac codes with BMI ≥35 floors. Managed decline: the TrumpRx oral Wegovy maintenance dose fell from $299 to $199 (Jul 2029), Foundayo to $149–249, and injectable semaglutide/tirzepatide cash to $249–349. Retatrutide (Lilly) cash runs $299 starting to $449 at top doses, the only branded product above $349, with a list price ~$1,450. Boehringer's survodutide adds a third seller from Sep 2029. PBM 'metabolic formulary' deals pushed net prices down an estimated 12–15% over two years. Orals are ~49% of users and ~58% of new starts. The gray market regrew from ~3M to ~8.2M users through 503A 'personalised' telehealth compounding, offshore pharmacies and 'research-use' retatrutide vials ($90–180/month) that circulated before and after its approval.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Mar 2029)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved Jul 2029)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus; AUD indication Feb 2030)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and cardiovascular disease (tirzepatide; confirmatory trial ongoing)
alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide, Feb 2030); ASAM guideline endorsement (Jun 2029)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction using injectables and tirzepatide, which are still off-label for AUD
dementia-prevention use without cardiovascular disease, cash-paid on orals
microdosing for 'steadiness', now often paired with scheduled drug holidays
gray-market retatrutide for cosmetic 'recomp' cuts by lean young men
nicotine and gambling reduction: observational support only
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: Retatrutide was under review at the start of the window. Lilly approved Mar 2029 at the extended date, with ~28.7% mean loss at 80 weeks on top dose, dysesthesia and heart-rate warnings, and a REMS-lite titration guide. This honours the triple-agonist driver: surgical-grade loss from a pen. Survodutide (filed Jun 2028) was approved Jul 2029 and launched Sep 2029, positioned on MASH. Oral semaglutide AUD: phase 3 read out Oct 2028, filed Jan 2029, approved Feb 2030 (13 months). Amycretin filed Jul 2029; decision due no earlier than Q3 2030 and extended into 2031, so it is not on the market. MariTide phase 3 readouts came in 2030; it has not been filed and is not on the market. Bimagrumab-type muscle adjuncts are still phase 3; none approved. No oral matches tirzepatide. Global incretin market ~$150B (2029).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Retatrutide's top doses show higher early discontinuation (~9% for adverse events).
Elevated with rapid weight loss; more cases on retatrutide in line with greater loss.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The hip-fracture HR (~1.3 in 65+ long-term users) replicated in a 2029 Danish registry. Concern is rising about retatrutide, whose greater loss brings proportionally more lean loss without resistance training. Sarcopenia is concentrated in older women, cyclers and gray-market users without counselling.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 2028 class warning and CMS DXA code remain; retatrutide label requires baseline DXA consideration at 60+.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: A 2029 pooled analysis of US, Nordic and Korean cohorts (~9M users) found HR ~2.1, or roughly 2–4 excess cases per 100,000 person-years. Across ~68M US users that is ~1,400–2,700 excess cases a year, mostly permanent partial vision loss, with higher risk in diabetics and people with sleep apnoea.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class warning (Oct 2029) across all incretin labels, upgraded from EMA's 'very rare' wording. Patients are told to report sudden painless vision loss; ophthalmology societies advise a baseline eye exam for high-risk users.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the AUD trial population.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Interim postmarketing data (2030) put clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7–9% of users versus ~3% of controls, ~11% on top-dose retatrutide. The effect is dose-related and reversible on dose reduction. It is widely self-managed with drug holidays.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing study continuing; AUD label mentions mood monitoring; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months. Regain after retatrutide is faster in absolute kilograms.
More case series, concentrated among gray-market and high-loss retatrutide users.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; adolescents on decades-long therapy; repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up. No adolescent peak-bone-mass data yet; the first pediatric DXA postmarketing readout is due 2031.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone postmarketing requirement in force.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, unapproved molecules)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~11,500 cumulative FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product by mid-2030. Retatrutide 'research' vials are the fastest-growing category, with tachycardia and dosing-error calls. Poison-centre incretin calls are ~4× 2025 levels. No mass-casualty contamination event repeated the 2028 cluster.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alert continues; warning letters to telehealth storefronts; personal-importation enforcement still weak.

safety_ledger.effect: Dysesthesia / skin hypersensitivity and heart-rate increase (triple and glucagon-containing agonists)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Dysesthesia in ~8–20% of top-dose retatrutide users, mostly mild and transient; mean resting heart rate up ~5–7 bpm.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled on retatrutide and survodutide at approval; cardiovascular outcomes trial required.

food_and_beverage.state: About 40% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~8–10% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~8%. Dollar sales are flat to slightly down as price-pack architecture runs out of room. Protein and fibre lines are mainstream. Discount chains in lower-income areas still sell full-size packs; upscale grocers in high-adoption suburbs have cut centre-store space by about a tenth.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~12% from 2025 and beer ~7%. The AUD approval and ASAM endorsement turned off-label prescribing into insured treatment. Heavy drinkers, the core revenue base, fell fastest. Brown-Forman and Constellation have cut US capacity further, and non-alcoholic and 'occasion' lines grow but do not replace the lost volume. Tavern closures in mid-sized Midwestern cities continue.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and checks are smaller. Small-plate, protein and 'half-portion at 70% price' menus are standard. Steakhouses do well among the lean-and-lifting tier; buffets and dessert chains keep closing. Bar revenue at casual-dining chains is down double digits.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking, while mainstream brands add 'athletic cut' and small-muscular fits for the top-tier body and stretch ranges for cyclers. Two markets have split: premium tailoring for the retatrutide-lean and value stretch basics for everyone else. Resale volume of barely worn larger sizes floods thrift.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Boutique 'muscle-protection' studios with DXA scanners cluster in affluent zip codes; budget gyms add racks but not coaching. Employer metabolic tracks still bundle gym check-ins.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage fell to 31%. Pharmacy trend is ~+8% a year, driven by AUD, cardiac and dementia codes that employers cannot easily exclude under parity and benefit rules. Plans run diagnosis-integrity audits of 'AUD upcoding'. Wellness premium differentials persist outside Illinois. PBMs sell 'holiday-tolerant' adherence verification that allows scheduled pauses.

pharma.state: Lilly and Novo dominate, with Boehringer a small third. Retatrutide is the growth product. Net US prices drift down 12–15% through PBM and cash-channel deals, but volume rises faster. Ex-US prices keep falling under generics. Brand-protection spending against gray-market retatrutide is a growing cost line.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body now reads as a pay stub. Lean with visible muscle and good skin means branded drugs, DXA scans, a trainer and protein. A sharp, slightly gaunt leanness reads as gray-market vials without coaching. A regained or never-treated large body reads as off coverage, not as appetite.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Class stratification has hardened into uniforms. In Phoenix, 'Scottsdale lean', the muscular retatrutide-and-lifting look, is a professional expectation in real-estate, sales and finance offices. In Maryvale and the West Valley warehouse belt, bodies divide between cash-oral users, vial users and people who never got access. Upper-income adolescents are the most medicated youth cohort. Weight is no longer read as willpower; it is read as plan design.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are short. Hosts plan for 'half-hungry' tables, and holiday drug holidays are now a planned part of the calendar. The Bread Alone church fasting network claims ~700 congregations. Dinner as the main social event is giving way to walks, lifting sessions and coffee.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps show 'on', 'off' and 'on holiday'. Body type signals income on profiles in a way users discuss openly and resent. Desire mismatch remains a common presenting issue; couples synchronise drug holidays for anniversaries and trips.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has become a marker of class and of mood. Clinics treat it as noise. The Unmuted collective treats it as life. Working-class commentators increasingly treat a visible appetite as authentic and lean muscle as a sign of privilege, a framing MAHA-adjacent influencers and fat-acceptance revivalists both use.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Measured clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~7–9% of users (~11% on top-dose retatrutide) versus ~3% of controls. Surveys suggest about a third of users have taken at least one deliberate dose reduction or drug holiday to 'get the colour back'.
interior_life.framing: The industry still sells 'steadiness'. Users now call it 'the flat' and joke about it in public. Talk-show monologues and TikTok formats ('first night off holiday') have made it a shared complaint rather than a private side effect. Clinicians treat it as dose-adjustable. The AUD indication cuts the other way: for heavy drinkers the blunting is the treatment.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Adherence-verified tracks still cover ~3.5M employees, but vendors now permit scheduled two-week holidays, because rigid tracks produced dropouts and the EEOC charges went into conciliation. Managers talk about 'holiday weeks' when some staff are irritable and hungry. Sales and creative firms quietly discourage top-dose regimens, and logistics and call centres still prize steadiness.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off nights' have gone from the Unmuted collective's Philadelphia and Brooklyn shows to bar promotions in Austin and Chicago, timed to common holiday windows. Flat fiction has a backlash genre of 'hunger' memoirs. Sportsbook handle among identifiable users is still down. Comedy about 'the flat' is a staple.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Drug holidays cluster around weekends, honeymoons and anniversaries, which drives cycling. Couples therapists report fewer mismatch complaints from synchronised couples and more from couples where one partner is on top-dose retatrutide.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The complaint is mainstream, but no legislation followed. California's adherence-premium bill stalled in committee in 2029, and no new state acted. The left–right coalition now campaigns on class, arguing that the lean body has become a benefit of good insurance. Still no measurable effect on turnout.

state.regulatory_posture: Continuity without new initiative. FDA approved retatrutide, survodutide and the AUD indication on schedule and issued the NAION class warning, but no new state action reshaped access. The import alert and warning letters continue at the same tempo while the gray market outgrows them.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate and no new subsidy. TrumpRx cash prices continue and stepped down through manufacturer deals. The Bridge pilot was not revived. The 2027 tri-agency premium guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: PBM fill data and app-linked logs still feed wellness vendors, now with 'approved holiday' flags. Five state employee plans still cover weight-loss drugs only via monitored tracks. Two Medicaid programmes still tie continued coverage to adherence and BMI. Payers audit AUD diagnoses for upcoding.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE is unchanged. The Army's supervised oral pilot for recruits continues. Trucking firms now route drivers to on-label oral AUD treatment; DOT still has not ruled.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply most global semaglutide, and China is the main source of gray-market retatrutide peptide. US–India talks still feature CBP mail enforcement. US cash prices run ~10–30× Indian generics, narrower than in 2028.

events.event: FDA approves Lilly's retatrutide after an extended review; label shows ~28.7% average weight loss at top dose with dysesthesia and heart-rate warnings; cash launch at $299–449 a month
Novo and Lilly cut TrumpRx maintenance prices (oral Wegovy $299→$199; injectables to $249–349) as Boehringer's survodutide nears launch and PBMs sign 'metabolic formulary' rebate deals

FDA warning letters hit 140 telehealth storefronts selling 503A-compounded 'personalised' semaglutide and 'research-use' retatrutide; analysts estimate 8 million Americans now use non-approved product
Pooled analysis of 9 million users finds doubled NAION risk; FDA orders class-wide optic-nerve warning on every incretin label
Business Group on Health survey: employers covering weight-loss drugs fall to 31%, with remaining coverage tied to diabetes, cardiac and BMI ≥35 criteria
FDA approves oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder, months after ASAM guideline endorsement; Medicaid and Part D coverage follow under prior authorisation

open_tensions: The AUD indication opens an insured door that weight loss no longer has. Payers are auditing 'AUD upcoding' while parity law and Medicaid rebate rules make the indication hard to exclude, and Part D spending (~$35B a year) climbs with no budget vote.

Retatrutide delivers surgical-grade loss to those who can afford $449 or a coach, and to gray-market buyers who get the molecule without the DXA, titration or eye exam. The NAION warning and lean-mass warning fall hardest on the second group.

Drug holidays are now mainstream, while adherence-conditioned premiums, regain physiology and the chronic-therapy model all assume continuous use. Vendors' 'holiday flags' paper over the conflict without settling it.
Body shape has become a visible readout of insurance tier. The first adolescent bone-density data, due 2031, will land on a cohort that is mostly upper-income.

prose.headline: The Lean Line: In 2030, You Can Read an American's Health Plan From Across the Room
prose.world_in_600_words:
One American adult in four is now taking an incretin drug, about sixty-eight million people. Close to a third have tried one. The rise came while the old route to these drugs, employer coverage for weight loss, kept closing. Fewer than a third of large employers still pay for weight management, usually only above a BMI of 35 and often only for employees who let a vendor watch their refills. The growth came through other routes.

The first is price, which came down slowly. Last July Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly cut the government cash-channel price of the daily Wegovy pill's maintenance dose from $299 to $199. Starting doses still cost $149, and the printed $1,349 list price is ignored. Injectables sell for cash at $249 to $349. A third seller, Boehringer, arrived with survodutide, and PBM rebate deals trimmed net prices by a few percent each year. Nothing here is cheap, but a pill now costs about the same as a phone plan.

The second is retatrutide. Lilly's triple agonist was approved in March 2029, after a long argument about tingling skin and racing hearts. It takes off nearly thirty percent of body weight at the top dose, as much as a sleeve gastrectomy, from a weekly pen. At $449 a month with a coach, a body scan and a protein plan, it produces a particular look: lean, muscled and clear-skinned. In Scottsdale offices that look is now simply expected. In the West Valley the same molecule arrives as a 'research peptide' vial from a website, for about a third of the price, with no DXA scan and no titration schedule. About eight million Americans now use product the FDA never approved. Warning letters go out and the parcels keep coming.

The third is alcohol. In February the FDA approved oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder, half a year after the addiction physicians' society endorsed it. That made the drug something insurers find hard to refuse. Parity law covers commercial plans, and Medicaid and Medicare must cover it under prior authorisation. Plan auditors now study how many new drinking diagnoses arrive with a BMI of 38. Spirits volumes are down about twelve percent from 2025. The heaviest drinkers, who bought most of the bottles, were the first to stop.

The safety record grew alongside the market. The optic-nerve risk once called very rare now has a class warning on every label. Large pooled cohorts show the risk roughly doubled, which means somewhere between fourteen hundred and twenty-seven hundred extra Americans a year lose part of their sight. Patients now get an eye-exam leaflet with the pharmacy bag. The bone and muscle warning from 2028 still applies, and it hits harder on a drug that removes this much tissue.

The flatness has moved from HR decks into everyday conversation. Users call it 'the flat'. About a third have cut a dose or taken a deliberate holiday to feel things again, around a wedding, a trip or a weekend. Bars in Austin and Chicago advertise 'off nights' timed to the common holiday windows. Wellness vendors, which used to count every missed refill, now issue 'approved holiday' flags, because rigid tracks were losing people and two EEOC charges went to conciliation. California's bill against adherence-conditioned premiums stalled, and no other state acted.

What is left is a country that can read itself. A big body used to suggest appetite; now it suggests a lapsed plan. Gaunt leanness suggests vials. Lean muscle suggests money. Snack aisles are smaller, plus-size stores keep closing, and budget gyms have racks but no coaches. Adult obesity has fallen to about a third. Most of the improvement is real, and so is the way it is distributed by income.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Ortega wakes at 5:40 in Tolleson, takes the white pill with a sip of water and waits thirty minutes before coffee, as the leaflet says. The pill costs her $199 a month through the TrumpRx app since her dental-billing office dropped weight coverage in January. Her husband Héctor keeps his vials in the butter compartment. They came from a site that calls them research peptides. He pinches his belly, injects, and says his skin hums all morning.

At work, Dr. Kessler comes in from his six o'clock lift with forearms like rope and asks whether the Hendricks claim cleared. Marisol notices she is cataloguing bodies again: the hygienist, soft at the jaw since spring; the new front-desk girl, sharp-boned, probably vials. She hates that she can tell.

At lunch she eats half a torta and wraps the rest without thinking about it.

The pharmacy text says her refill is ready. The bag has a new yellow sheet: *Sudden painless vision loss — call immediately.* She reads it in the car twice, then photographs it for Héctor.

Tonight she starts her holiday. Her daughter's quinceañera is Saturday, and Marisol wants to be hungry for her mother's mole and to cry at the waltz instead of watching herself not cry. Her app will log the pause as approved. She has already asked her sister to save her two tamales.

At 9 p.m. she puts the blister pack in the drawer with the passports, turns off the kitchen light, and stands there a moment, waiting to feel hungry again.
